messages.subject: dealing with correlated parameters
parts:
Hi,

Is there some trick to re-parametrize the model where parameters are highly correlated:
    for (i in 1:N) {
        eta[i] <- - elasticity * log(1 + distancex[i] / a) +
            A[origin[i]] + B[destination[i]];
        log_lik[i] <- neg_binomial_2_log_log(flow[i], eta[i], phi[i]);
    }
It appears that parameters a and elasticity are highly correlated.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: dealing with correlated parameters
parts:
Thanks a lot.  Do you think this will work?

parameters {
    vector [N] log_phi;
    real <lower = 0> sigma_phi;
    vector [2] z; // vector, the entries of which are given independent unit normal priors
    cholesky_factor_corr [2] L_Omega; // Omega is correlation matrix for random effects
    vector <lower = 0> [2] sigma_u; // random effect sd
}
transformed parameters {
    real a;
    real elasticity;
    vector [N] eta;
    vector [N] log_lik;
    vector [N] phi;
    vector [2] u; // random effects

    u <- (diag_pre_multiply (sigma_u, L_Omega) * z); // generate random effect
    elasticity <- exp (u [1]);
    a <- exp (u [2]);
    phi <- exp (log_phi);

eta [i] <- - elasticity * log (1 + distancex [i] / a) +...
        log_lik [i] <- neg_binomial_2_log_log (flow [i], eta [i], phi [i]);
    }
}
model {
    z ~ normal (0, 1);
    sigma_u ~ cauchy (0, 2.5);
    log_phi ~ normal (0, sigma_phi);
    sigma_phi ~ cauchy (0, 2.5);
    increment_log_prob (sum (log_lik)); 
Thank you,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] dealing with correlated parameters
parts:
Assuming A and B are parameters, you'll also find them correlated because
there's an additive non-identifiability.

Always use log1p(x) instead of log(1 + x) --- it's always faster and
it's more arithmetically stable when x is near 0.

- Bob
